name: Plinest

lead: Plinest is a sterile viscoelastic gel from the Italian company Mastelli whose main component is highly purified polynucleotides (PN HPT). It is injected into the skin in a clinic as a so-called skin booster.

The appearance goal is better-hydrated, firmer, smoother-looking skin, including on the neck and decollete, and softening of acne scarring. The manufacturer describes hydration and support for skin that has lost elasticity, firmness or tone [1]. A 2026 observational study of 66 patients treated with three sessions reported clinician-rated visible improvement in facial skin [2].

paras: A clinician injects small amounts of the gel into the skin in a series of sessions spaced a few weeks apart; Mastelli's professional page describes courses of two to three sessions depending on the target, using fine needles [1]. It is sometimes combined with other injectables, as in a 2025 three-patient case series of a mixed product that included Plinest [3].

Injection-site effects such as redness, swelling and bruising are the usual concerns with intradermal injectables; the 2026 observational study monitored spontaneous adverse events [2]. Plinest is described as a CE-marked class III medical device, and the manufacturer lists it for healthcare professionals only [1][2].

angle.text: Used as a skin booster to improve hydration, firmness and fine texture, and on acne scars, according to the manufacturer. Treatment is performed by clinicians in short series of sessions.

lead: Plinest is a sterile, single-use viscoelastic gel for intradermal use whose main component is Polynucleotides HPT, with a 2% polynucleotide concentration (40 mg in a 2 ml prefilled syringe) [1]. It is made by Mastelli Srl of Italy [2].

The product is used for skin rejuvenation. Mastelli says it provides hydration and support for skin with loss of elasticity, firmness or tone, and lists younger skin and acne scars as indications for the face [1]. A 2026 observational study describes it as a CE-marked class III device for the face, neck and decollete [3].

Published data are small. A real-world observational study followed 66 adults across 106 treated areas using the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale and clinician scales [3], and a 2025 case series reported on three women treated with a combined product containing Plinest [2].
infobox: Face; neck and decollete in studies [3]

paras: Plinest consists of water, polynucleotides (2%) and phosphate salts and is supplied in a 2 ml syringe with fine needles [1]. The manufacturer says it is intended for healthcare professionals [1].

Mastelli says the gel hydrates and supports skin with reduced elasticity, firmness or tone, may help remodel areas with a strong fibrous component such as acne scars, and improves turgor and elasticity [1].
The 2026 observational study monitored safety through spontaneous adverse event reporting [3]. As with other intradermal injectables, local reactions are the usual concern.

A 2026 observational data collection in 66 adults who received three intradermal sessions reported clinician-observed visible improvement in 100% of facial areas, using GCI-S and GAIS [3]. A 2025 case report of three women aged 44 to 59 used a combination protocol that included Plinest, hyper-dilute Radiesse and Profhilo, and assessed outcomes six months later; the authors note no prior data on that combination [2].
